en.title: Minimum Count of Non-Endpoint Values in a Subarray with Equal Ends
en.description:
A contiguous subarray of length at least 2 whose first and last elements are equal is valid. Its variance is the subarray length minus the number of its elements equal to the endpoint value. At least one valid subarray is guaranteed to exist; find the minimum variance.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n; the second line contains the array. 2≤n≤200000, elements 1..10^9, and at least one value repeats.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: Example 1: the range 1, 2, 1 has only one element that is not 1, so the answer is 1. Example 2: the two 5s have nothing between them, so the answer is 0. Example 3: there are 2 other elements between the two 1s and also between the two 2s, so the answer is 2.
hints: For each value, only compare adjacent occurrences: take their index difference minus 1, and keep the minimum.
